grammar.title: Saying prices in the hundreds and thousands (百 / 千)
grammar.pattern: Number + 千 + Number + 百 (+ Number + 十) + 塊
grammar.explanation: To say big prices you build the number from the biggest unit down: 兩千八百塊 (2,800), 一百二十塊 (120). 百 and 千 always need a number in front of them — you must say 一百, 一千, never just 百 or 千. For 2, Taiwan Mandarin uses 兩 before 百 and 千: 兩百, 兩千. Add 多 after the unit for a rough amount: 三千多塊 (three thousand-something).
grammar.contrast: 兩 vs 二: use 兩 when counting an amount (兩千塊, 兩張票); use 二 only inside a number's tens/ones position (十二, 二十五) or when reading digits out one by one, like a phone number.
grammar.common_error: Learners say 二百塊 or drop the 一 and say 千塊. Say 兩百塊 and 一千塊 instead.

passage.title: 我們的旅遊
passage.hanzi: 上個月我和哥哥去旅遊。我們先上網買飛機票，一張要兩千八百塊。那天早上我們搭捷運到機場，飛機很快就飛到台東。第二天我們坐船去看魚，風很大，可是那裡真的很漂亮。我們一共用了五千多塊，可是都玩得很快樂。
passage.gloss: Last month my older brother and I went on a trip. First we bought plane tickets online — 2,800 dollars each. That morning we took the MRT to the airport, and the plane got us to Taitung very quickly. On the second day we took a boat out to see the fish. The wind was strong, but the place was really beautiful. We spent five thousand-something dollars altogether, but we both had a great time.

grammar.title: 一……就…… (as soon as / whenever A, then B)
grammar.pattern: Subject + 一 + V/Adj + 就 + V/Adj
grammar.explanation: 一……就…… links two things that happen right after each other, or a habitual reaction. The subject comes first, before 一. Use it for body and weather reactions: 我一累就想睡覺 (whenever I'm tired, I want to sleep). Both clauses share the same subject here; if the subjects differ, put the second subject after 就: 天氣一陰，我就不想出門。
grammar.contrast: 因為……所以…… also links cause and result, but it explains one single situation ('because it rained, I didn't go'). 一……就…… says the second thing follows the first immediately or every time. If you mean 'every time / the moment', use 一……就……; if you are giving a reason for one past event, use 因為……所以……。
grammar.common_error: Learners put the subject after 一 (X 一我累就想睡覺) — the subject must come before 一. They also add 了 inside the pattern for habits (X 我一累了就想睡覺); keep it plain when talking about what always happens.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yí lèi jiù xiǎng shuìjiào.
examples.gloss: As soon as I get tired, I want to sleep.

examples.pinyin: Tā yì shēng bìng jiù bù xiǎng chīfàn.

examples.hanzi: 天氣一陰，我就不想出門。
examples.pinyin: Tiānqì yì yīn, wǒ jiù bù xiǎng chūmén.
examples.gloss: The moment the weather turns overcast, I don't feel like going out.

grammar.title: V + 一下 (do something a bit)
grammar.explanation: 一下 after a verb makes the action short and casual, and softens requests: 休息一下 (rest a while), 看一下 (take a look). It is very common in spoken Taiwan Mandarin.
grammar.contrast: 一點 also means 'a little', but it goes with adjectives or nouns (累一點、喝一點水), while 一下 goes after a verb to shorten the action.
grammar.common_error: Saying 我很休息一下 or putting 一下 before the verb (X 一下休息). 一下 always follows the verb, and you don't add 很.

passage.title: 週末的天氣
passage.hanzi: 上個週末，我和家人去台北玩。第一天是晴天，我們騎腳踏車，也去了夜市吃東西。第二天天氣很陰，還下了雨，走了很多路以後，媽媽很累，就在旅館休息。台灣不下雪，可是媽媽說，下次想去日本看雪。
passage.gloss: Last weekend my family and I went to Taipei for fun. The first day was clear and sunny; we rode bikes and also went to the night market to eat. The second day was very overcast and it even rained. After walking a lot, Mom was very tired and rested at the hotel. It doesn't snow in Taiwan, but Mom said that next time she wants to go to Japan to see snow.

grammar.title: Saying where something is: A 在 B 的 左邊／右邊／旁邊
grammar.pattern: A + 在 + B + 的 + 左邊／右邊／旁邊
grammar.explanation: To locate one thing in relation to another, name the thing you are talking about first (A), then 在, then the reference place (B), and put the direction word 左邊 / 右邊 / 旁邊 at the very end. 的 is often kept after a noun but is usually dropped after a short place word like 捷運站旁邊. 左邊 is 'to the left of', 右邊 'to the right of', and 旁邊 just means 'next to' without saying which side.
grammar.contrast: Compare with B + 旁邊 + 有 + A (「捷運站旁邊有一家書店」). Use 在 when the listener already knows what A is and you are telling them where it is; use 有 when you are introducing something new that exists there. So: 飯店在捷運站旁邊 (Where is the hotel?) vs. 捷運站旁邊有一家飯店 (What's around here?).
grammar.common_error: Learners reverse the order and say things like 「在左邊的銀行」 when they mean 「銀行的左邊」. In Chinese the reference point comes first and the direction word comes last: 銀行的左邊 = the left side OF the bank, while 左邊的銀行 = the bank ON the left.

examples.hanzi: 飯店就在捷運站的旁邊。
examples.pinyin: Fàndiàn jiù zài jiéyùn zhàn de pángbiān.
examples.gloss: The hotel is right next to the MRT station.

examples.gloss: That coffee shop is to the right of the post office.

grammar.title: 先…再… (first … then …)
grammar.pattern: S + 先 + V1 + 再 + V2
grammar.explanation: 先 marks the first action and 再 the one that follows it, so 先洗手再吃飯 means 'wash your hands first, then eat'. Both 先 and 再 go before the verb, never after it.
grammar.contrast: 再 here means 'then, afterwards' for a planned sequence, not 'again'. 又 means 'again' about something already finished: 他又看報紙了 = he read the paper again.
grammar.common_error: Learners put the time word after the verb, like 「我洗手先」, or replace 再 with 後. Keep both adverbs in front of their verbs: 我先洗手，再吃早餐。

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiān xǐ shǒu, zài chī zǎocān.
examples.gloss: I'll wash my hands first, then eat breakfast.

passage.title: 飯店的早上
passage.hanzi: 昨天晚上我們住進台北的一家小飯店。今天早上我洗好手，就下去吃早餐。餐廳在飯店的右邊，旁邊有一張大桌子，上面有很多報紙。我問服務生：附近有郵局嗎？他說郵局在銀行的左邊，走路十分鐘就到了。
passage.gloss: Last night we checked into a small hotel in Taipei. This morning, after washing my hands, I went down for breakfast. The restaurant is to the right of the hotel, and next to it there is a big table with lots of newspapers on it. I asked the attendant: is there a post office nearby? He said the post office is to the left of the bank, just a ten-minute walk away.
